timeline.event: The Nok culture makes terracotta sculptures in central Nigeria
timeline.label: c. 500 BCE

timeline.event: Artisans at Igbo-Ukwu cast intricate bronze vessels
timeline.label: c. 900

timeline.event: Lifelike copper-alloy heads are cast at Ife
timeline.label: c. 1300

timeline.event: Oba Ewuare the Great begins rebuilding Benin City
timeline.label: c. 1440

timeline.event: Sokoto is founded as the capital of a new caliphate
Richard and John Lander trace the Niger to the sea
Britain annexes Lagos as a colony
Flora Shaw coins the name 'Nigeria' in The Times
The Northern and Southern Protectorates are amalgamated
Oil is found in commercial quantities at Oloibiri
Chinua Achebe publishes 'Things Fall Apart'
Nigeria becomes independent from Britain
Nigeria becomes a federal republic
The naira replaces the Nigerian pound
Lagos hosts the FESTAC festival of Black and African arts
Wole Soyinka wins the Nobel Prize in Literature
The federal capital moves from Lagos to Abuja
Nigeria wins Olympic football gold in Atlanta
Nigeria returns to civilian rule and the Fourth Republic begins
Nigeria's first satellite, NigeriaSat-1, is launched

places.name: Lagos
places.clue: Nigeria's largest city spreads across islands and mainland around the Lagos Lagoon.

places.name: Abuja
places.clue: The planned capital, seat of government since 1991, lies beneath the granite dome of Aso Rock.

places.name: Kano
places.clue: An ancient Hausa trading city, famed for its old walls and the Kofar Mata indigo dye pits.

places.name: Ibadan
places.clue: This sprawling Yoruba city is home to Nigeria's oldest university and the landmark Cocoa House.

places.name: Benin City
places.clue: Seat of the Oba of Benin and home of the bronze-casters' guild on Igun Street.

places.name: Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove
places.clue: A UNESCO-listed forest on the Osun River, filled with shrines and sculptures.

places.name: Yankari Game Reserve
places.clue: Bauchi State's wildlife park, known for elephants and the warm, clear Wikki Spring.

places.name: Niger-Benue confluence
places.clue: Nigeria's two great rivers meet beside Lokoja, forming the 'Y' on the national coat of arms.

places.name: Calabar
places.clue: The old Efik trading port hosts a December carnival billed as Africa's biggest street party.

places.name: Sukur
places.clue: A hilltop chiefdom in the Mandara Mountains with terraced fields and stone paths, a UNESCO site.

places.name: Igbo-Ukwu
places.clue: Excavations here uncovered intricate bronzes from around the 9th century.

places.name: Chappal Waddi
places.clue: Nigeria's highest peak, about 2,419 m, rises in the Gotel Mountains on the Cameroon border.
